draft.title: Education and training
card: Government spending on schools, universities and vocational education and training (VET) is a budgetary supply-side policy. It aims to lift the skills of the workforce.
Skills and knowledge gained through education and training are called human capital. A worker with more human capital can produce more in each hour of work.
Higher labour productivity means more output from the same amount of labour. It lowers the cost of each unit produced and raises the economy's productive capacity.
Better skills also help workers move into jobs where skills are in short supply. This can ease skill shortages. The effects usually build up slowly, over years.
draft.remember: Education and training spending builds human capital, which lifts productivity and capacity over time.

a.q: Why does government spending on vocational training act as a supply-side policy?
opts: It raises worker skills, so each hour of work yields more
It raises household spending, so firms sell more goods now
It lowers interest rates, so firms borrow more to invest
It cuts the price of imports, so firms pay less for inputs
a.why: Training builds human capital, so workers produce more per hour and capacity rises. A short-term lift in spending is a demand-side effect, which is the tempting wrong answer. The policy works by improving the quality of labour.
a.clue: Think about what training changes about the worker.

b.q: Victoria funds more TAFE places for trade apprentices. Which result would best show the policy is working, even though it takes years?
opts: Output per hour worked rises in the trades over time
Unemployment falls sharply in the first month of the program
Trade workers' wages are frozen by the government
Demand for trade services falls as the program grows
b.why: Better skills show up as higher labour productivity, which lifts capacity. A fall in unemployment within a month is unlikely, because the effects of education and training usually build up slowly. Frozen wages and falling demand are not signs of higher skills.
b.clue: Look for the measure of output from each worker over time.

a.best: It raises worker skills, so each hour of work yields more

b.best: Output per hour worked rises in the trades over time
